correctness.rationale: Writing the fractional-remainder numerators as y,y,x with x congruent to -2y modulo P splits the unique Hamilton allocations into two strict regions: the small state receives the unique surplus seat for 0<y<P/3, while the two equal large states uniquely receive the two surplus seats for 2P/3<y<P. Since a=(P-c)/2, advancing one house sends y to y+a without wrap in the first region; the transition crosses to the second region exactly when y>(P+3c)/6. That inequality also keeps the small state's lower quota fixed, so it loses one seat. The integer count of residues in the open interval is the displayed ceil/floor formula. A fresh independent exact Hamilton replay over 127 primitive pairs with a<=20 matched the theorem, including (3,3,1), (7,7,2), and (9,9,1).
risks: Cutoff-tied house sizes are intentionally excluded; the theorem does not assign a random or deterministic tie-breaking convention there.

value.rationale: This gives an exact infinite-family solution inside a rational regime explicitly singled out as delicate because seat changes are periodic and ties matter. The tie-independent formulation isolates convention-free losses and yields both their exact residues and frequency.

final_claim: For primitive populations (a,a,c) with a>c>0 under Hamilton apportionment, tie-independent Alabama losses occur exactly when (P+3c)/6 < (ha mod P) < P/3, P=2a+c, giving the stated exact count and periodic frequency; only the smaller state loses.
limitations: Three states with two equal larger populations only.
